name: psu_bank_pairs_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: PSU (Public Sector Undertaking) banks share nearly identical business models, regulatory frameworks, government ownership, and macro sensitivity. SBI, Bank of Baroda, PNB, and Canara Bank exhibit 0.65-0.80 daily correlation — among the highest in any Indian sector — because: (1) government policies affect all PSU banks simultaneously (recapitalization, merger mandates, priority sector lending), (2) they compete for the same customer base with similar product offerings, (3) RBI rate decisions impact them identically (similar CASA ratios, NIM sensitivity). When one PSU bank diverges from the group (e.g., SBI reports good numbers but PNB lags on a day with no PNB-specific news), the laggard catches up within 30-60 minutes. This is the tightest pairs opportunity in Indian equities due to the exceptional homogeneity of PSU bank fundamentals.
universe: SBI, Bank of Baroda, PNB, Canara Bank
stock_filter: SBI: ADV > ₹500 crore. Bank of Baroda: ADV > ₹150 crore. PNB: ADV > ₹100 crore. Canara: ADV > ₹80 crore

data.index: NIFTY 50, NIFTY Bank, NIFTY PSU Bank

indicators.name: group_correlation
indicators.formula: mean of all pairwise rolling_corr(stock_i, stock_j, 60) across 4 stocks

conditions: no stock-specific news for the lagging stock
no stock-specific news for the leading stock

exit.target: stock_deviation reverts to 0 (back to group average)

risk.position_sizing: ₹1L on divergent stock (directional on stock, hedged by group mean expectation)

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 25 (PSU banks are rate-sensitive; high VIX correlates with rate uncertainty)
filters.time_filter: no trades first 15 min or last 15 min
filters.volume_filter: divergent stock volume > 50th percentile of its typical
filters.trend_filter: no trend filter (group mean reversion is trend-independent)
filters.event_filter: skip during result season for any PSU bank, RBI policy day, government recapitalization announcements
other_filters: skip if divergent stock has NPA/provision headlines

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — PSU bank homogeneity is structural (government ownership, similar business models). Unless privatization significantly differentiates them, the correlation will persist.

weaknesses: PSU bank stocks can gap significantly on NPA/provision news for individual banks, creating overnight risk that bleeds into the next day's intraday correlation.
Government actions (merger announcements, recapitalization) can permanently change the relative value of PSU banks, invalidating the equal-weighted group mean.
PNB and Canara Bank have lower liquidity than SBI, creating execution challenges and wider slippage on the divergent stock when it's not SBI.
prior_art: Avellaneda & Lee (2010) 'Statistical Arbitrage in the US Equities Market'. In India, PSU bank correlation is documented in NIFTY PSU Bank index methodology. Srivastava & Joshi (2016) study government ownership and stock correlation in India.
notes: The directional (unhedged) approach works because the group mean reversion is strong enough to predict the divergent stock's direction. A market-neutral version would use SBI as the hedge leg against the divergent stock, but this requires larger capital allocation. Consider switching to NIFTY PSU Bank futures as hedge when available.
